newsitem.title: GERMANY: Moscow has access to NATO codes-German magazine. [CORRECTED 12:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Moscow has access to NATO codes-German magazine. [CORRECTED 12:25 GMT]

text.p: Russian intelligence has access to an internal NATO communications system after the KGB paid U.S. National Security Agency (NSA) employees in former West Berlin to betray the secret codes, a German magazine reported.

Citing internal NSA reports, Focus said in a report released ahead of publication on Monday the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) was investigating six former NSA employees over the alleged security breach it said took place at the end of the Cold War. (Corrects full name of FBI from "Federation Bureau..." to "Federal Bureau...")
Focus also said its own research had shown that the coded communications system in question, the analogue Secure Telephone Unit system, was used by German intelligence as well as by NATO leaders.

It quoted a former officer from East Berlin's Ministry for State Security (Stasi), Horst Maennchen, as confirming that Russia's Federal Intelligence Service, the successor to the Soviet Union's Committee of State Security (KGB), had cracked NATO's codes and still had access to the internal system.
The report could not be confirmed independently on Sunday.
The NSA was at the centre of a recent investigation in the United States that led to the conviction of a former NSA clerk for selling state secrets to the Soviet Union 30 years ago.

Robert Lipka was found guilty of photographing documents while working at headquarters at Fort Meade, Md., between 1965 and 1967 and handing them over to the KGB. He was jailed for 18 years and fined $10,000.
